$comment: Canonical identifier rules shared by mxlpy and mxlweb-core. Every exporter that turns a model name into code (mxlpy -> mxlweb model.ts, mxlweb -> mxlpy/python/JS/WAT) maps names through `canonical`, so the same model has the same ids in Python and JavaScript. A canonical id matches `pattern` (ASCII only: WAT locals are `$id`) and is not in `reserved`. `canonical(raw)`: (1) return raw if already canonical; (2) Unicode NFKD, drop combining marks (category M*); (3) replace each character found in `transliterate`; (4) replace each `-` that ends a token (followed by a character outside [A-Za-z0-9] or the end; regex `-(?=[^A-Za-z0-9]|$)`) by ` minus `, then each character in `symbols` by ` <word> ` (a `-` between letters/digits is a hyphen and handled by step 6); (5) strip leading/trailing runs outside [A-Za-z0-9_]; (6) replace each remaining run of non-alphanumerics that contains at least one character outside [A-Za-z0-9_] (regex `[^A-Za-z0-9]*[^A-Za-z0-9_][^A-Za-z0-9]*`) by a single `_`; (7) empty -> `_`; (8) leading digit -> prefix `_`; (9) result in `reserved` -> suffix `_`. Mapping a whole model (`canonical_map`): every name maps to canonical(name); two names of one model mapping to the same identifier is an error, never resolved by renaming. Consumers vendor `reserved`, `transliterate` and `symbols`; their drift tests compare against this file, and `tests/identifiers.fixtures.json` holds the cross-language cases.
